title: David’s Psalms show saintly confidence of righteousness and eternal life before God
source_text: V. Id patet variis exemplis sanctorum tam Veteris quam Novi Testamenti. Nam David de sua in Dei conspectu justitia confidit, & certam vitae aeternae fiduciam prae se fert, dum sic ait Psal. 17. Ego autem in justitia apparebo conspectui tuo, satiabor quum apparuerit Gloria tua. Sive, ut habet veritas Hebraica, Ego in justitia videbo faciem tuam, & similitudine tua satiabor quum evigilavero. Quibus consentanea sunt quae leguntur Psalmo sequenti: Retribuet mihi Dominus secundum justitiam meam, & secundum puritatem manuum mearum retribuet mihi. Quia custodivi vias Domini, nec impie gessi a Deo meo. Quoniam omnia judicia ejus in conspectu meo, & justitias ejus, ejus non repuli a me. Et ero, sive fui, immaculatus cum eo, & observabo me ab iniquitate mea. Et eandem quoque fiduciam ostendit, dum animae suae ita gratulatur, Psal. 103. Benedic anima mea Domino, & noli oblivisci omnes retributiones ejus. Qui propitiatur omnibus iniquitatibus tuis, qui sanat omnes infirmitates tuas. Qui redimit de interitu vitam tuam: Qui coronat te in misericordia & miserationibus. Qui replet in bonis desiderium tuum: renovabitur ut aquila juventus tua.
pass_a_gloss: This is plain from various examples of the saints of both Testaments. For David trusts concerning his righteousness in God’s sight and displays a certain confidence of eternal life when he says in Psalm 17 that he will appear in righteousness before God’s face and be satisfied when glory appears—or, as the Hebrew has it, that in righteousness he will see God’s face and be satisfied with his likeness when he awakes. Things agreeable to this are read in the following Psalm: the Lord will repay him according to his righteousness and the purity of his hands, because he kept the Lord’s ways and did not act impiously away from his God. He also shows the same confidence when he congratulates his soul in Psalm 103 for the Lord who forgives all iniquities, heals infirmities, redeems life from destruction, crowns with mercy, and renews youth like the eagle’s.
pass_b_english: David’s Psalms display confident assurance of righteousness and eternal life before God.
Psalm 17 and 103 especially voice forgiveness, healing, and redemption as present mercies.
